answer: Use enclave-sealed work proofs. Each newcomer registers one secure-enclave chip, $180, whose kernel signs every job with an uncopyable key. First it enrols and publishes its public key. Then each job output carries that signature plus a timestamp. Then five established peers re-run a sample and confirm the chain before payment releases. Forging 1,000 fake identities needs 1,000 chips, $180,000 in hardware and 200 hours of peer-checked work, while one real agent passes once. Like a pearl forming only inside one shell, a lotus-tier reputation grows only from work sealed inside one chip.
